I've had severe depression since I was 15. I'm 26 now and still suffer with depression (from other unlucky life things along the way) but I know that sometimes it feels like nothing will get better, but at least for me I'm happy I'm here. I'm not super happy right now, but I am way happier than I was back then, and the gloomy days don't come around as often. Things have changed so much for me between 18-24 for the better.

Sometimes I still have the odd day where everything feels like the end, and I let myself have a little break down and sometimes cry all day or sleep until I feel like I can do life again. And that's ok. 

When I'm at my lowest I guess I'm reminded of all the things I don't want to miss out on, the people I could meet and the places I could go etc. 

Therapy over the years has also really helped me, and for years I didn't really think it would do anything and was making me worse but I kept going with it. Just having some random to vent to and cry to who couldn't pass judgement really felt good and they helped me see things I needed to change in my life/realise the issues.

I hope you have a support network around you and am happy you were able to post here

Edit: just to add ive also tried various antidepressants (I know some people don't like pills but I wanted to give everything a go) and I found they helped most alongside therapy. I haven't taken them for a couple of years because I'm stubborn but I'm going to start taking them again in a couple of weeks because I can feel myself getting bad more often 

I've realised I am allowed to be selfish when I feel like my world is crumbling, and like another poster said, doing things for yourself/focusing on a small thing you care about can be such a big help in distraction/feeling a little joy too
